name: Video Luma Range
description: Evaluates per-frame luminance dynamic range and tonal distribution against photometric expectations to detect the compressed or artificially expanded intensity ranges typical of neural video synthesis.
algorithm: Video Luma Range — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes video luminance range for forensic detection:

1. **Dynamic Range Analysis**: The luminance range (minimum to maximum luma values) is measured per frame. The method checks whether the content uses the expected luma range for the video standard (broadcast range 16-235 for BT.601/709, full range 0-255 for full-range content).

2. **Range Consistency Check**: The luma range should be consistent across the frame and over time. The method detects regions with different effective dynamic ranges — composited deepfake faces may show different dynamic range (from the generator's output mapping) than the original background footage.

3. **Highlight/Shadow Clipping Analysis**: The behavior of highlights (near maximum luma) and shadows (near minimum luma) is analyzed. Natural camera capture produces characteristic clipping characteristics. AI generators may produce different highlight/shadow rendering — either clean clipping (missing the natural rolloff) or extended range (values the capture format shouldn't contain).

4. **Temporal Range Evolution**: Dynamic range typically remains stable within a scene. The method tracks luma range statistics over time — sudden range changes without corresponding scene changes indicate processing artifacts.

5. **Gamma/Transfer Function Analysis**: The effective transfer function (gamma curve) is estimated from the luma distribution. Different cameras and generators use different transfer functions. Mismatched transfer functions between face and background reveal content from different imaging pipelines.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through video luma range analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
